original.description: Objective: To design a solar array concept allowing for in-orbit reconfiguration of strings length and section size and to optimisethe solar array power output for EOL best possible performance.Description: Solar cell voltage and current are a function of operating temperature and degradation level. String lengths and section sizes are optimised for EOL best performance. However, this means that for most of the time the solar array is not exploiting its full performance capability. If string lengths and section sizes were reconfigurable, the power output at each time of the mission could be maximised. This concept could provide various benefits, such as flexible adaptation in case of unforeseen events (e.g. solar flares, micrometeorite impacts, etc.), mission extension in GEO and potential use of cells with less performance in GEO radiation environment. These benefits can be of interest for Telecom applications, where very large solar arrays are typically required to compensate for the degradation over the entire mission. This activity targets innovative photovoltaic assembly concepts that allows for reconfiguring string lengths and section size to optimise performance in dependence of operating conditions during the mission (e.g. temperature, irradiation level). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of a solar array / photovoltaic assembly concept allowing for reconfiguration of string lengths and section sizes. - Prototyping of interconnection concepts. - Initial proof of concept demonstration.

original.description: Objective:To characterise spacecraft materials that minimise atmospheric impacts during re-entry.Description:ESA's Green Agendaand Ecodesign Policy require that the environmental impacts of all space missions andprogrammes are assessed and reduced across their full life cycle. Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation.
